Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Guys, come and look at this. This is an actual replica of an artist's interpretation of what some random guy of no significance believed that the chariot of Asparagus might have looked like. And this is Asparagus, the greatest warrior in all of Greece. With this golden chariot, he would win every race. And here he is defeating the Minotaur, a creature that's half-man, half-bull. Asparagus defeated him using the head of Medusa, a creature so ugly she could turn people to stone with just one look.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: 1957! You place your shiny, hard-earned nickel into the coin slot! Think of it: all your favorite bands playing all their greatest hits at any time you want! You make your selection, guiding your chosen 45-RPM disc onto the magical turning table, center stage! Then, like a gentle nurse, an arm holding a needle lowers itself and finds its way into the groove! You turn around knowing the song you've chosen more than anything else tells the world what you're all about!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, so many things, really. Music, hobbies, you kids. Ooh! You know what she really likes, is my famous rhubarb creme brulee. I used to make it for her all the time when we were dating. Oh, it made her so happy. (Candace leaves but Lawrence doesn't notice her leaving.) You know, I should get out my toque and blowtorch and make one for her today. What a good idea, Candace. Thank you. (notices Candace has left) Candace? Well, all right then.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, actually there is one thing that you probably won't be able to find here. An 1807 Dorcham and Wesley Boot Scraper, only one of them was ever made, (dramatically) and it's been lost to the mists of time! Oh, if only I could find that, I'd be the envy of the entire antiquing community; especially Worthington Dubois, (he clenches his fists) my antiquing nemesis!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (To three songbirds) Look at that, my fine feathered friends! (He mounts his handiwork onto the tree trunk) Not a bad bit of work, even if I do say so myself. Just wait till you see the hidden surprise. (He pushes a red button on the front of the bird house, which bears the words 'home tweet home'. Its walls spring outward, revealing various miniature items including a fountain and a spiral staircase) Wha- nothing? Not even a sausage? No matter. (He pushes the button once again and the birdhouse folds back to its normal state) Wait until Linda and the kids see it. It'll blow their tiny minds. Well, not their tiny minds, that's not fair.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (reading) "Thank you for coming here today to hear my speech on the history of the ancient Ornithorhynchan tribe. (At this point, Candace's eyes begin to become heavy and she tries in vain to stay awake.) The Ornithorhynchans were a platypus-worshipping society known for painting themselves teal-blue and wearing elaborate platypus-themed costumes for their various dances and rituals."

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Linda! I don't know what's come over me, but I'm starting to get the most wild and uninhibited ideas! You know how every day for the last twenty years I've relaxed with a nice cup of Earl Grey? Well, not today, Linda! Today, I'm putting out all the stops! Darjeeling!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, this? It's an escape chamber from an old vaudeville show. In the old days, men would go into these things and pretend to be locked inside and then they'd "escape" to the amazement of the crowd. Here, let me show you. (goes inside the chamber) You see? All you need to do is just... (tries to escape) Ummm

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, that's the question isn't it? Only one of these can be the true Dorcham and Westley. And no doubt a wrong choice will trigger a nasty booby trap. Boot scrapers were famously vengeful people. This could take every ounce of antiquing knowledge that I possess.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: You know, kids, this theater was built over 70 years ago in this Neo-Egyptian style. (He buys the tickets and they walk inside) And apparently, there used to be a whole pharaoh's tomb display with a mummy in a sarcophagus. I mean, you couldn't pick a better place to watch a classic, old mummy movie.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, let's have a look then. Oh, oh, yes. I've seen this before. It's a commemorative coin from the nineteen hundred and three Danville World's Fair. Many steam-driven devices were introduced to the world back then. It must have been quite an event...

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, yes and I'm British, so you think I'm supposed to like bird watching. (Imitating a British accent) "Oh, I'm British, so I'll in the conservatory with a cup of tea and a crumpet." I'm saying that ironically but actually that sounds quite good. So I'm going to do that. Ta.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (inspecting the hole) Whoa, this doesn't look too good at all. Kids, don't come up here! It's far too dangerous! Mum and I will fix the boat. Candace, why don't you look for some food? And, boys, you could find us some shelter if you like. We may be here for a while.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: This statue, which stands outside the Whiskershire Rectory, still holds the Earl's actual spring stick, yes. The spring stick is used as such: it's placed in front of you so as to spring the hidden mousetraps to avoid capture. Now some suggest—

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: OK, now let's see. "Lead the way for the lovely lady with an elegant wave of your hand. "For you and only you, insert your name here..." Oh, thanks for the light. Hey! No, no, wait! No, no, help me put it out! Do something!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, your mother's jazz trio has a gig at the Mayor Day festivities, and I shall be running the antiques auction, oh yes! I'm very excited as we have a collection of steamrollers on the block, all imported from England.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, I did. Yes, of course I did, although she doesn't really care about this stuff. Anyway, they're practically giving 'em away online! D'you know, it's even more exciting than the Oklahoma land rush of 1889!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Ooo, those crazy kooks! I'll just do an old-school drop knee-turn on the bottom, eh? Cut back up the face, through the sloop, do a nice little tail slide, and drop into the green room for a bit of tube time.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, it's hard to explain actually, taking the flip pass from the winger, shoulder deking the defense men, and then, tossing it right over the old glove hand. Oh, it just takes hold of you like a fever!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Splendid! Then I'll set the scene: (Phineas and Ferb stand onto a circle spot which is an elevator. The elevator goes down) A chilly April morning, 1980. (As he speaks the elevator descends) Disco was on the way out and it had just begun to dawn on everybody they looked absolutely ridiculous in every photo taken of them in... (The elevator stops and dings, and it's door opens)

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: As was I until the other night, when my motorcar began behaving oddly. Suddenly, I-I saw a terrific flash of light. I-I was inexorably drawn to it and there was no escaping its irresistible magnetism

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Right here, son. (straining) I did manage to find my first edition of Caveman Man, the world's first prehistoric comic book carved out of granite. Just having a little less luck finding my spanner.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh yeah, brilliant. But I better check with Mum about this. (At phone) Uh, hello honey, yes, yes, oh gosh, I love you too, darling. Uh, are you aware the boys have a monster truck in the backyard?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, your mother's going to meet a lot of exciting and cool people. What if I'm...I'm no longer cool enough for your mum? I'm hardly a rock star, am I? (walking away sadly) I"m afraid I'm hopelessly nerdy.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh! My word, there's a truck-driving pharmacist and he's pressing his face up against his windshield. Oh, that's what I love about you Americans. You-You're like big, fun children.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: What? Everyone knows that boy would rather be somewhere else. What about you two? The crops are so far ahead, would you like to spend the rest of the summer at swim camp on Naboo?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: It's such a waste to get rid of them. See? Look. Chopsticks and ponzu sauce. That's Japanese but-but look, there's also a Chinese fortune cookie! That's what's known as 'fusion'.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (On screen) Oh, the kids are going to love this Austrian-style cuckoo clock. Oh, I wish you'd let me buy the large one. (The Melt-inator fires, melting the tires of the car and making Linda scream) Maybe we should pull over and see what's going on. (cut to them examining the flatness) That's peculiar.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (sighs) That didn't go over as well as I'd hoped. Mmmm, perhaps I need to spuh-ruce it up more! Sprrrrrruce! Sprrrrrrrrrrrrrr—Ahh! Ooh! Ow! I do believe I've sprrrrrrrained my elbow.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, that was the best Father's Day flight yet! It brought back some some wonderful old memories and created a lot of new ones. Thank you, boys, for making this possible!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well here we are gang, the semi-annual Tri-State Area antique show and swap meet. Here you can find anything under the sun, literally, because it's held outdoors. Ha, ha.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And here, we have a marvel 16th century wardrobe. We had one just like this when I was a schoolboy. And inside it was another land filled with magical woodland creatures.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, Candace there's no such thing as lots of things, and there's such a thing as many other things. (Spins the steering wheel) Is Nosey such a thing? (The car stops turning) Well, you see, that's the thing, isn't it?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, excellent. Well it's good to see you boys taking an interest in Greek mythology. I'm doing the same. I've got over 12 hours of gladiator movies here I wanna watch.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, you'd be surprised, what with Steamroller Today magazine and Wacky Steamroller videos posted on the Internet. The public is going crazy for the flattening arts.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: What did I come in here for again? Was it my Bench Warmer baseball cards, or this photo of me kicking an orange, or my sculpture of the world's happiest jackalope?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Ah, don't distract her, Candace. She was up all night trying to finish this book for her book club. But if we're having donuts, let's get the glazed ones, too. Ha!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, look. This T-Rex footprint was found not 30 yards from this very spot. Hey, and it says here that this fossil was dug up right near our very own neighborhood.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Thank you for coming here today to hear my speech on the history of the ancient Ornithorhynchan tribe. The Ornithorhynchans were a platypus-worshipping society...

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Yeah, mom and I are getting rid of a few old things at the antique store, but I think I've got just what you need. (a moment later...) A snow cone machine just like when I was a kid!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Look at this. I got a traffic ticket from that camera they installed across the street. Oh, that blasted device picks up everything on the block 24 hours a day.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And that is why the 18th century sewing thimble was not only a slice of history, but a compelling example of American grit and perseverance. Hmm? Hmm? Hmm? Yes?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Look, boys; it's your cousins visiting from England! They're here to see the exhibition football match between Danville and their beloved Snifferton Nostrils.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, we couldn't very well serve that cake, the way those wild penguins tore it apart, could we? And to think that they were carried away by a freak tornado!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, yes, you have fun at the castle party tonight. (putting the mask on his head) If you need anything, your mother and I will be here scaring the sugar out of the little trick-or-treaters.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (Gasps) By Harry! That's Boot Scrape! The secret language of the ancient boot scapers. (Reading) To gain the world, and halt the wintle, reverse your mind, and mind the lintel.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, the ship held together pretty good, didn't it? (shift to reveal he's holding the wheel surrounded by debris from the wreckage.) Of course, we'll have to re-attach the wheel (shift to reveal the sloop on a rock.) and fix that, uh, giant hole. Now, kids, are you all right?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, hehe, there you are. (to Ignatius) Um, I'd like you to meet my wife Linda, and our kids and their friends. Everyone, this is Ignatius Ukareamü, my old college chum.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, go on. Play track three! It's the one where a group of truckers take down a corrupt police force using only their trucks and their saucy colloquialisms.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Say, there is something pretty peculiar going on here, now, don't tell me! You've turned the entire garage upside-down, now why on earth would you do that?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Yes, the Boot Scrapers were renowned for their elaborate spiral staircases. If that Dorcham and Westley Boot Scraper still exists, we'll find it down here.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Your mother's favorite band. **(rock ballad)** Love Händel. (Flashback to Linda and Lawrence in the crowd in a huge stadium, looking much younger and wearing very 90's clothing.) I bought us tickets to their farewell concert. Oh, we were a handsome, stylish couple back in those days.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Uh, L-Linda, my dear, I love you, but you couldn't have chosen a worse moment to go completely bonkers! I'm sorry, but I've got to call you back! Bye!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: I said, "John, it's great, I love the tune but the words. 'All you need is a Phillips head screwdriver', it just doesn't really ring true, does it?" (Phineas and Ferb reappear on the boat.)

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Kids, this is miraculous! I love the book-evator and the book slide, and... Oh, my, is that a leather-bound first printing of Kafka's Metamorphosis?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh dear, the poor thing. Look at that. Wait a minute. Antidisestablishmentarianism? That's more of an ideological stance than a disease. Isn't it?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (on the car with Phineas, Ferb, Candace, Linda and Perry, going around Piccadilly Circus) Ooh! Merry old England. How I love our yearly holiday to my parents' home. Big Ben, Buckingham Palace, oh, the White Cliffs of Dover. Stonehenge.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Alright, I want to see everyone out there on the dance floor. Parents, kids, giant robots, sure why not? Let's kick this party into second gear!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Boys, I've got some good news for you. I've arranged for you to play a little exhibition match between periods at the Danville Ice Trays game.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: The Cavern of Secrets. This entire room was made from materials scraped off the boots of Danville Elders, who were highly creative engineers.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (He examines the scroll) A Dorcham and Westley Boot Scraper's map! But only three of them were ever made,(dramatically) and they were lost to the mists of- oh I'm doing it again.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Hello, just calling to say good luck on your test. Imagine the newfound freedom you'll have if you don't fail! Which, of course, you won't!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: I thought so. Yes, easy-peasy, that one. Next, the tip of a shoelace. Yes, yes, that little hard tip at the end of a shoelace is... Honey?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Soon, the entire village of Whiskershire began following the Earl's lead to, of course... (phone rings again) Uh, do forgive me. I-I-I'm awfully sorry. Hello?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, it's not actually called a boat, darling, it's called a sloop. When we're at sea there's no right or left, only port and starboard.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, hold your horses, kids. It says here that the lead of Cirque de Lune has a severe allergy. They're canceling today's performance.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Hmmm, visual aids. Ah, that's how I can (rolling his r's) sprruce it up a little. Sprrrruce! Sprrrrrruce! Spuuuuuuuuh-ruce! Ha ha ha, ah, very good then.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And here's the 17th century Whiskershire spring stick, which belonged to the Earl of Whiskershire. (A man dressed in royal garments and a mouse costume appears on screen. Lawrence's phone rings.) Oh, 'scuse me for a second. Hullo.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, how nice! A traditional Christmas special. As my Granddad used to say: "Lung me yellum reek and wits fulgey an'ool bool bay-a!!"

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (at the kitchen) Ah, yes. The Daily Crossword puzzle. Today's theme: "Tip of the Day". 1, across; The metal tip of an umbrella. Let's see... honey?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: It's the new, digitally remastered third series of Pinhead Pierre! Only the best series ever of my favorite show ever! That's all.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, just a few vocal exercises before my big speech for the committee of the Danville Museum. Would you like a little sneak peek?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, rapture! This is my favorite part of the Danville Harbor Day's festival! The annual shark reenactment. Let's checketh it out.

Name: Lawrence-2
Dialog: Boys, what are you doing here? You'd better get inside before the Doofbot catches you. I'm off to the factory. See you next week!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, that's not very nice, is it? But look on the bright side, Candace, this year we might take home one just like this. Ta da! (Makes a W with his three fingers on his forehead)

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: I can do that? Hey, I don't remember seeing this part. Hmm, (Laughs) well, it looks just like Candace. Hey, honey, you've gotta see this!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, boys, we're off to the Center for Historically Relevant Botanical Gardens, a virtual treasure trove of topical topiaries.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, I can't believe it! It seems my video traffic ticket's been cleared. I guess there is someone up there looking out for me.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, dear, it looks like everybody's found themselves something to do, and our Chez Afrique dinner reservation's in an hour.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Is it really? (pauses) How remarkable. Well, we're the Flynn-Fletcher family. Two adults, three children, (holding up a pet carrier with Perry inside it) and our pet platypus, Perry.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, what a phenomenal finale to our finale. Congratulations and kudos to our two winners. And there wasn't even a contest.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (Walks in) Oh, hello, boys! Are we having a party, Baljeet? And Baljeet and. . . wait a moment, if he's Baljeet then you must be. . .?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (Chuckles) Pinhead was the best! And I happen to own the single greatest collection of Pinhead Pierre paraphernalia in all the world.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, my favorite bookcase finally gave up the ghost. A lot of these I should get rid of, but some of them are my favorites.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: See, Candace? Even a trained professional has trouble from time to time. Now, I want you to just relax, and park this car!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Hello. we had the most amazing time. Look! I found this 19th century barometer. Anything interesting happen 'round here? (There's silence for a moment)

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Why yes, yes it is! Jeremy, you have your license, don't you? You can take Candace for a ride in it when it's finished.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Okay, well, be sure to be home in time for the barbecue. We're gonna be watching Kermillian's Comet fly past the Earth.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Such beauty, such tranquility. A fisherman's paradise. Yes, of all the lakes in the world, I'm glad we picked the Nose.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Do you know, Candace, I don't remember much of what happened here today, (hugs his daughter) but I'll never forget this moment with you.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (Chuckles) Well... (Dashes off and comes back wearing fishing gear) If I must. (Camera zooms into him) Well, who knows? I might even be persuaded to tell you a few of my world-famous fishing stories.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And Lot Number 5 is sold to the woman in red. And now the last item of the day: we have Lot 6. Do I have any bids?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, it took three hours for them to untangle my hair from the gears, but I never lost my grip on that lava lamp.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Right-o! (runs to get it) It's been at my bedside all these years! (pushes coffee table over) Hop on, boys! (all sit on rug) We're about to take off on the ride of a lifetime!

Name: Lawrence-2
Dialog: Well, I don't suppose there's any reason to hide this stuff anymore. So, yes! As they used to say, "Have a ball!"

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Kermillian's Comet was named after an ancient Danville astronomer, Augustus Kermillian, who discovered the comet.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Okay, kids. I'll leave you in charge of the machine and be easy on your sister. She's been a bit on edge lately.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Ah, my university chum, Ignatius, has been trying to get us to visit his animal research station for years now.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, I think it's rather sweet that Betty Jo and Grandpa Clyde invite you kids and all your friends every year.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And just to express how sorry we are, here's my credit card. You have our permission to ruin us financially.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Hey, you know, kids, these fossils are of creatures that lived right here in Danville millions of years ago.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: What-What, this? Oh, no, no, no, no, no, no, I have all the confidence. This is, uh, this is just in case...

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Hmm... and this leads directly to the 1960s. (unplugs the jukebox) Oh, well, time to get this beaut to the antique shop. (wheels it away) Ta, boys!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And now, ladies and gentlemen, what you've all been waiting to bid on. I give you, the antique steamrollers! (crowd cheers)

Name: Lawrence/Max
Dialog: You know, I feel strangely comfortable like this. But how can I be a rock star if nobody's ever heard of me?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Yes, but fat lot of good it did me. I mean here we are, thirty years later and they've lost our reservation.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Okay, I'll decide where we go on vacation as soon as I clean out Perry's litter box. (looks into the litter box with the Hawaiian islands drawn on it) Hey, how about Hawaii?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, uh, let's move on, shall we? This next exhibit is kindly Old Man Simmons— Hey! Who's up for milkshakes?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, hi honey, we were just listening to some records. It's what we used to use for music when we were kids.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: No dear, the bird took a left at Snores-ville, and is up here in Danville. Can I get one up high? (Candace high-fives Lawrence) Woohoo!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (leads them into the garage) Oh, yes. It's the same car I had when I was a lad. I figured it would be ready when you were old enough.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, I'll let you in on a little secret: I let him win all these contests; look how happy it makes him!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (on CB radio) Yes, yes, this is Cheeky Monkey. You're shaking the windows. What's your handle, good buddy? Come back.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: I say, boys, you can barely feel the road! It corners like a dream! Pinhead Pierre, eat your heart out!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, kids, it's wonderful. The big one wouldn't have fit in the library anyway. Oh, I found my spanner!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Okay, honey, but don't press the red button on it, will you? I want to be there when you see it, okay?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: ...and their kids, Beckham, Beckham, Pele, Beckham, Pele, and Eliza. Well, her middle name is Beckham.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Okay, Candace. All you have to do is park between this plastic trash can, and that plastic trash can.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, yes, we're ready for our journey of self-discovery while crawling through the belly of the Earth.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, well, so much for that. I guess it's not a total loss. I mean, this is still presentable, right?

Name: Lawrence Robot
Dialog: Jolly good, Candace. As long as it's okay with Mum, it's okay with me. Stiff upper lip and all that.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: ...So he said, "Try ignoring it and hope it goes away. (Camera zooms into them) And do you know what? It did. After 17 weeks.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, you can say what you like about Candace, but there's nothing primitive about her imagination.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, it's my favorite kids show from when I were a lad. Oh, they don't make them like this anymore.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: I'll be right there, sweetheart, I'm just clearing a spot for the trophy we're going to win today.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, I'm sure you're going to hear plenty more fantastical stories during Gran and Gramp's visit.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And we'll love them anyway. Candace, the sooner we get started, the sooner we all get to go home.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (he rolls his tongue) Hello, hello hello! Can you guess what my DJ costume is for tonight's big Mardi Gras block party?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (to Linda) Oh, and another little tidbit about the ancient Egyptians (Doofenshmirtz and Perry run past them in the background) is that both men and women wore makeup.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh, the spirit of Danville, see how his sole gleams, the Boot Scapers took their craft seriously.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, let me see... He had some kind of a German accent, and ooh, he was also wearing a lab coat.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: That's why our couch cushions are worn so unevenly. 'Cause we're always on the edge of our seats.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Okay. (on CB radio) Uh, breaker, breaker, 1-9. This is Cheeky Monkey. Anybody got their flappers on out there?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh no Buford, they were real. They were tiny rooms where you could talk on the phone in private.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Look! The Lengthiest & Most Thorough Adventures of Lord Ramblington has been made into a movie.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (yelling to Linda) Dear! Are you aware the boys have turned the garage upside-down, looking for Ferb's skateboard?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Ahem. Look, darling, I'm in the middle of something right here, so I'll have to phone you back.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Look, I'm telling you, it's the most peculiar thing I've ever seen. It looks just like Candace.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Cool, isn't it? I was inspired to put it out of storage after my well... (clears throat, whispers) ...my close-encounter.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (opening the box) Oh, my! An exact replica of Father's biplane! Oh, it's perfect! (giving his daughter a hug) Thank you so much, sweetheart!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, I'm a little rusty on my Hawaiian, but here goes. Buenos dias, señor. Me llamo Lawrence. (Spanish: Good day, sir. My name is Lawrence.)

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And that is why we celebrate Harbor Day every year with a reenactment. Here cometh the shark.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: It was either back up the fire escape or lose the pants altogether. Then suddenly it hit me.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Honey, I'll have you ladies home in two shakes of a lamb's tail. (Tires screech) Whoo! That was a close one.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Well, it turns out it was a tow truck driver I called. He changed my battery, and I was off!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Why does everyone guess that? No, I'm a Mardi Gras jester. Speaking of which, where's Perry?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Yes, indeed. Often you had to negotiate various booby traps that were set centuries before.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: And Lot Number 2 is a little beaut from Aveling & Porter built in 1924. Do I have any bids?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: All right, then. I'll clear all these drawers and boxes out later, darling. See you, boys!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Ah, there's the rub. Right next to the pair of ducks. I'm also packing this book of puns!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh! That was close. (rights the car back up) Whoops! Dropped my address. (picks up the paper) Well, (places paper on the sun visor) 6106, Palindrome Road, here I come!

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Wish me luck, boys. (at the mechanical mother) Hello, old dear, so lovely to see you. (bows) I've brought you some peonies. (pulls out a bouquet)

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Yeah, sure. Hey, did you know they've just found a cure for antidisestablishmentarianism?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Uh, I can see it right here, darling. Just need to give it a little... (twists, but some water squirts on him.) Oh, dear. Oh, my.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: I did, didn't I? Well, I suppose I get melodramatic when I start talking about antiques.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Why don't you hang onto her 'til next year? I've got no room left in the garage anyway.

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: (pauses video) You see, right there. Modern cartoon shows never ask the really big questions, do they?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Oh I see you like that little doll. Well lets see... that'll cost you, uh, fifty cents?

Name: Lawrence
Dialog: Turn the thing right-side up and come in the house. I believe I've solved your mystery.

Name: Lawrence-2
Dialog: Back in the old days, before Youknowwho, people used to use this stuff to play sports.

Name: Lawrence
